title: Manage cleaner credentials and property visits
intro: Keep the cleaner’s shared evidence, company role and recorded visits connected to the work your team manages.
description: Keep the cleaner’s shared evidence, company role and recorded visits connected to the work your team manages.
requirements: The person and cleaning company assigned to the work
Training required for the cleaning task
The evidence your organisation needs to review
review: Set requirements for the actual role and property. Identify which records the cleaner holds and which your company maintains. Review the supplied evidence and record the reviewer, decision and next action. A shared profile should not imply that every qualification, background check or employment condition has been independently verified.
work: Use recorded check-ins and check-outs to review visits associated with a worker and site. When the team changes, review the new person’s evidence before the next assignment. Agree separately who may enter the property, hold keys and act on customer instructions.
boundary: A work profile gives the recipient information to inspect. It does not prove property-access permission, prevent impersonation or guarantee safe conduct.

title: Prepare temporary-worker evidence for placement
intro: Review temporary-worker evidence against the placement before handing the record to the next decision-maker.
description: Review temporary-worker evidence against the placement before handing the record to the next decision-maker.
requirements: Required qualifications, induction and check evidence
review: Record who is responsible for each check and what evidence the agency and client maintain. Review the result against the actual placement rather than universally clearing the worker for every job. Keep outstanding evidence and conditions visible to the person arranging the assignment.
work: Follow placement review dates and recorded arrivals. A changed worker, role or requirement should prompt a review of the affected evidence. It does not follow that every shift requires a new statutory right-to-work check.
boundary: Agency and hirer responsibilities depend on the arrangement and current guidance. Certifyd organises records; it does not automatically complete statutory checks or determine liability.

title: Review electrical-worker qualifications and visits
intro: Connect the electrical worker to the qualifications and site requirements your organisation needs to review.
description: Connect the electrical worker to the qualifications and site requirements your organisation needs to review.
requirements: The scope of the electrical work
The company responsible for the assignment
review: Different electrical tasks can require different evidence. Record the qualification, certificate or registration inspected, its source and the reviewer’s decision. One generic verified label should not imply that every installation, inspection or building-regulation requirement has been satisfied.
work: Keep the worker’s record connected to recorded site visits. If another person attends, review the substitution and evidence relevant to their role. Use genuine credential expiry dates or a separate company review date to plan the next action.
boundary: Certifyd does not certify an electrical installation or automatically query a professional scheme. Your organisation reviews the requirements and completes any scheme or competence check through the appropriate source.

title: Review plumber evidence and recorded site visits
intro: Review the evidence needed for the plumbing work and keep it with the person assigned to the property.
description: Review the evidence needed for the plumbing work and keep it with the person assigned to the property.
requirements: The tasks included in the assignment
The worker’s company and review responsibilities
review: Match requirements to the task. General plumbing and gas work are different scopes; do not imply that the same evidence authorises both. Record the source or register checked where one is required, the result and the reviewer. A supplied certificate and the company’s check record serve different purposes.
work: Record arrival and departure where site check-in is part of your process. Review replacement workers against the applicable requirements. Keep expiry dates attached to credentials that actually expire and use company review dates for your own policy.
boundary: A shared profile or arrival record does not certify the work, establish gas competence or authorise entry. Your company uses the appropriate professional source and makes the assignment decision.

title: Manage construction-worker records by role and site
intro: Keep named workers and subcontractors connected to the evidence required for the job and site.
description: Keep named workers and subcontractors connected to the evidence required for the job and site.
requirements: Site induction and required safety evidence
review: Define evidence requirements for each construction role rather than treating everyone on a crew as interchangeable. Your company maintains site inductions and review decisions while workers share personal credentials. Keep the source, date and outcome of each relevant check with the person’s record.
work: Review recorded arrivals and departures by site. If the crew changes, identify the new workers and revisit requirements relevant to their tasks. Attendance information does not establish continuous presence, appropriate supervision or permission to perform every activity.
boundary: Certifyd does not replace construction safety management, certification schemes or prescribed right-to-work checks. Your organisation determines and reviews the requirements for the actual work.

title: Review care-worker evidence and visit records
intro: Give the care team a route from role requirements to worker evidence, review decisions and recorded visits.
description: Give the care team a route from role requirements to worker evidence, review decisions and recorded visits.
review: Separate personal training certificates from company-held evidence of suitability and right-to-work checks. DBS certificates have no official expiry date. Record check information and your review policy separately rather than inventing a universal three-year expiry. Keep unresolved evidence visible to the responsible reviewer.
work: Connect the record to care-site or home visits where relevant. For an agency replacement, review the actual placement and evidence responsibilities. Document status and attendance serve different purposes; neither replaces the provider’s supervision and safeguarding process.
boundary: Certifyd does not automatically confirm DBS status, notify families about every visit or guarantee safeguarding outcomes. Your care provider reviews evidence and makes the suitability decision.

title: Prepare agency-nurse evidence for placement
intro: Review the nurse’s evidence against the placement and retain the employer’s check records for the next reviewer.
description: Review the nurse’s evidence against the placement and retain the employer’s check records for the next reviewer.
requirements: The nurse, agency and clinical placement
review: Use the appropriate NMC employer process to confirm registration where required. Retain the result and date beside the supplied evidence. A document uploaded by the nurse is not the same as a current employer confirmation. Resolve unanswered questions before the placement decision.
work: Maintain placement review dates and site requirements as the assignment changes. Recorded arrivals connect the worker to a visit history while the team maintains its evidence and decisions. A shift check-in is separate from registration and statutory right-to-work checks.
boundary: Certifyd does not automatically verify NMC registration or decide clinical suitability. The agency and client retain their responsibilities for the actual arrangement.

title: Review security-guard evidence and site records
intro: Prepare the guard’s evidence for the assigned work and record the checks your organisation actually completes.
description: Prepare the guard’s evidence for the assigned work and record the checks your organisation actually completes.
requirements: The security activity and any licence requirement
Licence details and the check result
The employer’s decision and review date
review: Use the SIA’s tools and guidance to check the licence relevant to the activity. Retain the result, date and reviewer where your process requires it. Keep a supplied card or number distinct from the register-check outcome. Resolve any restriction or discrepancy before assigning work.
work: Connect company requirements and review dates to the worker. Recorded check-ins and check-outs can support attendance review but do not prove continuous guard coverage, authorised access or completion of a licence check at every shift.
boundary: Certifyd does not automatically query the SIA register or certify suitability for every activity. Your organisation uses the official source and makes the assignment decision.

title: Manage warehouse-worker evidence and attendance
intro: Connect the warehouse role, required evidence and company review to the worker attending the site.
description: Connect the warehouse role, required evidence and company review to the worker attending the site.
requirements: The worker and employment or agency arrangement
review: Define requirements by the work assigned. A general record should not imply authorisation for every vehicle, machine or task. Your company maintains induction and review decisions while workers contribute relevant credentials. Keep outstanding evidence visible before approving the assignment.
work: Review recorded site arrivals alongside worker evidence. When agency personnel change, follow the process for the actual placement and substitution. Record a prescribed employment check separately from attendance; check-in is not automatic right-to-work verification.
boundary: Home Office checks, labour-market duties and warehouse safety procedures have distinct requirements. Certifyd organises evidence and recorded activity; it does not replace those checks or guarantee compliance.

title: Prepare hospitality-worker records before a shift
intro: Bring role-specific evidence into view before the venue assigns a worker to a shift.
description: Bring role-specific evidence into view before the venue assigns a worker to a shift.
review: Use requirements appropriate to the task and venue. Your company maintains induction and review records while workers share personal training evidence. Record who performed prescribed employment checks and where their results are held; a uniform or roster entry is not that evidence.
work: Follow approaching credential dates and outstanding reviews without implying that every shift requires another statutory check. Recorded check-ins can support visit history. Payroll, hours, permitted work and supervision still need their respective review processes.
boundary: Certifyd does not automatically establish right to work at the entrance or determine agency and hirer responsibilities. Review the actual arrangement and appropriate evidence.

title: Review remote-worker evidence during onboarding
intro: Keep remote onboarding focused on the evidence, check method and decision your organisation needs.
description: Keep remote onboarding focused on the evidence, check method and decision your organisation needs.
requirements: Company policies, induction and review responsibilities
review: A video introduction and an uploaded document answer different questions from a prescribed employment check. Choose the appropriate method for the worker’s circumstances and jurisdiction, retain the result and record the decision. Keep organisational policies distinct from worker-held credentials.
work: Follow missing evidence, pending reviews and approaching recorded dates. Give the next reviewer a clear action rather than relying on one verified status. Discuss the access controls, existing systems and integrations your remote process needs before extending it across teams.
boundary: Certifyd’s records workflow does not authenticate meeting participants, detect deepfakes or establish legal identity from a device. Your organisation completes the required checks and security decisions.

title: Manage cleaner records across customer properties
intro: Keep cleaner evidence connected to company requirements and the properties your team assigns.
description: Keep cleaner evidence connected to company requirements and the properties your team assigns.
review: Set requirements before inviting cleaners to contribute evidence. Distinguish personal credentials from company inductions and decisions. When a worker or requirement changes, follow the affected record and assign the next review rather than relying on a general cleared status.
work: Review recorded property check-ins and check-outs. Where a shared profile is used, agree what person-and-company information the recipient should inspect. Company review records and customer instructions need access appropriate to the role and purpose.
boundary: Certifyd does not automatically give customers every worker document or revoke property-entry permission. Your company controls assignments, disclosures and access decisions.

title: Manage workforce evidence across hospitality venues
intro: Follow each venue’s requirements to the evidence and reviews behind an assignment.
description: Follow each venue’s requirements to the evidence and reviews behind an assignment.
requirements: Ownership of each check and decision
review: Keep evidence responsibilities clear across venues and labour suppliers. Review requirements for the actual role and arrangement rather than assuming one record covers every job. Your business maintains company documents and reviews while workers share credentials relevant to work.
work: Follow missing evidence, pending reviews and genuine expiry or review dates. Connect recorded attendance to venue visit history. Keep pay, working time, immigration permission and competence in their respective processes, with evidence supporting each decision.
boundary: The Fair Work Agency’s labour-market remit is separate from Home Office immigration enforcement. Certifyd does not automatically satisfy either body’s requirements or promise an inspection outcome.

title: Review workforce records across managed facilities
intro: Prepare client-site evidence while keeping worker, supplier and review responsibilities clear.
description: Prepare client-site evidence while keeping worker, supplier and review responsibilities clear.
review: Translate relevant site and contractual requirements into evidence your team can review. Distinguish supplier statements, worker credentials and your company’s decision. Where facilities differ, identify the requirements for each site rather than using a universal compliance status.
work: Connect recorded visits to the person’s evidence and company review dates. A changed worker, supplier or assignment should trigger review of affected requirements. Agree each organisation’s record access rather than assuming automatic chain-wide sharing.
boundary: Certifyd does not certify ISO, BREEAM or contractual compliance, or automatically grant building access. Your organisation reviews the obligations and makes the decisions.

title: Keep prescribed right-to-work evidence with reviews
intro: Choose the appropriate check, retain its result and connect the employer’s review to the worker record.
description: Choose the appropriate check, retain its result and connect the employer’s review to the worker record.
requirements: The prescribed method for the circumstances
The employer-facing result or document evidence
review: The Home Office guide explains manual and online checks, eligible right-to-work digital verification providers and the Employer Checking Service. A passport copy can form part of a prescribed check. An uploaded image, share code or QR scan does not itself complete the process or establish an excuse.
work: Use current guidance to determine whether a follow-up is required. EUSS settled and pre-settled status do not require repeat employment checks. Pending applications and verification notices have separate rules. Keep document expiry, permission dates and company reviews distinct.
boundary: Your employer or responsible organisation performs the prescribed check and decision. Certifyd organises records; it does not provide automatic statutory verification or immunity from penalties.

title: Review contractor credentials and site requirements
intro: Review contractor evidence against the work and site requirements before approving an assignment.
description: Review contractor evidence against the work and site requirements before approving an assignment.
review: Identify what the contractor supplies and what checks your company performs. Record the source, reviewer, date and outcome rather than using universally verified as an assurance. The actual contractual arrangement matters when determining employment and right-to-work responsibilities.
work: Connect the record to recorded visits and review dates. If another person attends, follow your substitution process and assess their relevant evidence. Keep site-access permission separate from attendance or an uploaded document.
boundary: Certifyd does not guarantee ISO 27001, SOC 2 or PCI compliance, automatically revoke access or prove legal identity from a device. Your organisation makes the check and assignment decisions.

title: Review agency-worker evidence and responsibilities
intro: Start with the agency and hirer arrangement, then record the evidence and decisions each party maintains.
description: Start with the agency and hirer arrangement, then record the evidence and decisions each party maintains.
requirements: The agency, employer, hirer and placement
review: Current Home Office guidance distinguishes arrangements; it does not impose automatic joint liability or duplicate checks on every standard agency placement. Identify the employer’s prescribed check and any evidence the hirer needs for its own obligations, role requirements or contractual assurance.
work: Connect shared credentials, company placement records and review dates. When a placement changes, review evidence relevant to that change. Site attendance can support a visit history but remains separate from the agency’s check and hirer’s placement decision.
boundary: Certifyd supports evidence and review work. It does not determine liability, certify every agency worker or replace the applicable prescribed check process.

title: Connect lone-worker records to assigned visits
intro: Connect worker evidence and company requirements to assigned visits and your separate safety procedures.
description: Connect worker evidence and company requirements to assigned visits and your separate safety procedures.
requirements: The separate risk and escalation process
review: Maintain the credentials and company reviews needed for the work. Keep personal evidence distinct from risk assessment, supervision and escalation procedures. A shared profile gives a recipient information but does not authenticate every person the worker will meet.
work: Review recorded arrivals and departures alongside the assignment. Check-in records a point in visit history; it does not prove continuous presence, wellbeing or delivery of an emergency notification. Agree separate contact, monitoring and response arrangements for the actual risk.
boundary: Certifyd does not replace a lone-working safety system or guarantee safety. Employers assess and manage risks through their own procedures.

title: Review worker suitability evidence and visit records
intro: Keep the evidence supporting a worker-suitability decision available to the responsible reviewers.
description: Keep the evidence supporting a worker-suitability decision available to the responsible reviewers.
requirements: The role, setting and safeguarding duties
The appropriate check level and eligibility
The reviewer’s decision and next action
review: Use checks appropriate to the role and jurisdiction. DBS, professional registration and right-to-work results answer different questions. Record what was inspected, when and by whom. Resolve concerns through your safeguarding process rather than inferring suitability from an uploaded document.
work: Connect evidence and company reviews to recorded visits where relevant. Give reviewers access appropriate to the purpose and role. Site events do not prove exactly who was present throughout the day or that every safeguarding requirement was satisfied.
boundary: Certifyd does not automatically confirm DBS status, authorise child collection or replace safeguarding decisions and response procedures.

title: Prepare nanny and au-pair employment evidence
intro: Keep hiring evidence and review responsibilities clear for the household or agency making the decision.
description: Keep hiring evidence and review responsibilities clear for the household or agency making the decision.
requirements: The role and actual employer or agency
Registration rules relevant to the jurisdiction
review: Use requirements appropriate to the childcare role and location. Registration rules differ by jurisdiction and circumstances; do not assume one UK-wide mandatory nanny register. Au pairs need appropriate work permission. A visitor cannot be employed as an au pair merely because they stay with a family.
work: Keep the decision and supporting evidence with the worker record. Use genuine credential dates and justified review dates. For an agency arrangement, establish what it checks and what the employer or household must decide.
boundary: Certifyd does not authenticate parents, authorise releasing a child or guarantee daily safety. Storing evidence does not provide immigration sponsorship.
